title: Cold Email vs the Spam Filter: The 3 Settings That Win the Fight
description: Own domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, open tracking off, and plain text at 30 a day. The 3 settings that keep cold email out of spam.
lead: This is the full guide from the reel. You get the 3 settings that win the fight with the spam filter, why each one works and exactly how to set it up.
insider: These 3 settings are the first thing we check on every client account. With them in place, one client sent **96,408 emails in five days with a 0.45% bounce rate** and booked 25 calls that week. The settings take an afternoon. Keeping dozens of inboxes healthy every week is the part we do for clients.

blocks.text: Gmail and Outlook decide in a split second if your email is real mail or spam. Usually the problem is not your copy or your list. It's your settings. Get these 3 right and you win most rounds before the reader even opens the email.

head: Round
Setting
Why it wins
rows: Your own domain + SPF, DKIM, DMARC
Removes a hidden image filters don't trust
Plain text, no links, about 30 a day per inbox
Looks like a normal person writing

blocks.text: Round 1: Your own domain, with ID

**Why it works:** a free address like @gmail.com looks like anyone could have sent it. In [Hunter's study of 31 million emails](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email), emails from a company domain got **5.2% replies vs 2.5% from free addresses**. That's about twice as many.
Your domain also needs 3 DNS records. Think of them as your ID card. [Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/a/answer/81126) ask senders to set them up.

head: Record
What it says
Where to set it
rows: "These servers may send mail for my domain."
"This email was signed by me and not changed."
"Here's what to do if an email fails SPF or DKIM."

items: Buy a separate sending domain that looks like your brand (for acme.com, try getacme.com). Don't use your main domain for cold email.
Add the SPF record your email provider gives you.

Turn on DKIM in your provider's admin panel, then add the record to DNS ([Google steps](https://support.google.com/a/answer/180504), [Microsoft steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/email-authentication-dkim-configure)).
Add a DMARC record. A simple start: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:you@yourdomain.com ([Google's DMARC help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/2466580)).
Check your setup with [Google's free Check MX tool](https://toolbox.googleapps.com/apps/checkmx/).

blocks.label: Watch your spam rate
blocks.text: [Google's sender FAQ](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14229414) says keep your spam complaint rate **below 0.1%** and never let it reach **0.3%**. Track it for free in [Google Postmaster Tools](https://postmaster.google.com).

**Why it works:** open tracking adds a tiny hidden image to every email. Filters see that on thousands of emails and get suspicious. In [Hunter's data](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email), emails with open tracking off got **7.4% replies vs 4.4% with it on**.

items: Open your campaign settings in your sending tool.
Find "Open tracking" (sometimes called "Track opens") and switch it off.
Also switch off link tracking. It rewrites your links through the tool's own domain.
Judge your campaign by replies, not opens. Replies are the number that pays.

blocks.text: Round 3: Plain text, no links, about 30 a day
**Why it works:** real people write short, plain emails to each other. No logos, no buttons, no links. And a real person doesn't send 500 emails a day from one inbox.

items: **Plain text only.** No images, no HTML design, no signature logo.
**No links in the first email.** Not even your website. Add it later, after they reply.
**About 30 cold emails a day per inbox.** Need more? Add inboxes, don't push one inbox harder.
**Warm up new inboxes first.** [Instantly recommends](https://help.instantly.ai/articles/5975329-how-warm-up-works-and-why-it-s-important) at least 2 weeks of warm-up before cold sending.

blocks.text: You want to send 300 cold emails a day. 300 ÷ 30 = **10 inboxes**. With 3 inboxes per domain, that's 10 ÷ 3 = 3.3, so **4 domains**. Each domain gets SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Tracking is off. The first email is plain text with no links.

head: What you see
Likely cause
Fix
rows: Emails go to spam right away
Fine for a week, then spam
Drop to about 30 a day, add inboxes
Turn tracking off and judge by replies
Wrong list or no easy way to opt out
Tighten the list and offer a simple opt-out line

blocks.label: Deliverability check prompt
blocks.text:
Act as an email deliverability expert. Here is my setup:
- Sending domain: [domain]
- Email provider: [Google Workspace / Microsoft 365]
- SPF record: [paste]
- DKIM: [on / off]
- DMARC record: [paste]
- Open tracking: [on / off]
- Links in email 1: [yes / no]
- Cold emails per inbox per day: [number]
- Inbox age and warm-up: [details]

Tell me which of the 3 rounds I'm losing (domain + records, tracking, plain text + volume), in order of how much each hurts, and give me the exact fix for each.

faq.a: No. Gmail and Outlook expect SPF, DKIM and DMARC from bulk senders. Start with p=none so nothing gets blocked while you check your reports.

faq.q: How will I know if people read my email without tracking?
faq.a: You won't, and that's fine. Replies tell you what's working. Opens were never reliable anyway, because many inboxes load images on their own.

faq.q: Can I add my website link in the signature?
faq.a: Leave it out of the first email. Add it in a follow-up or after they reply.
